findings.claim: Strategy's committed forward funding is zero. The $42bn '42/42' ATM authorisation announced 2026-03-23 is board approval to offer securities, not a pipeline: there is no backstop, standby purchase agreement or underwriting commitment. The obligations on the other side - $1,633m a year of preferred dividends - are contractual, cumulative for STRF and STRC, and ratcheting.

findings.source: Structural conclusion from the 42/42 announcement of 2026-03-23 and the absence of any disclosed committed facility in sources retrieved

findings.claim: Accretion from common issuance is $1 x (1 - 1/mNAV). At the November 2024 peak of 3.89x that was +74.3 cents per dollar raised; at today's 1.04x it is +3.8 cents, or about +2.3 cents after typical ATM fees - a 97% collapse in the value of the mechanism, which turns negative on a 5% share-price fall.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE

findings.source: Derived; mNAV of 1.04x from the Phase 1 NAV bridge, 3.89x November 2024 peak per market data

findings.claim: Preferred-funded bitcoin purchases carry an incremental margin of roughly minus 11 percentage points: a realised asset return of about 1% a year on Strategy's own six-year record ($63.73bn deployed, now worth $65.08bn) against a 12.00% STRC cost of capital. Growth here does not merely dilute returns, it destroys capital.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.source: Derived from Strategy's cumulative bitcoin cost basis and market value, against the September 2026 STRC rate of 12.00%

findings.claim: Bitcoin sales to fund preferred dividends have begun and are policy: 32 BTC sold 2026-05-26 to 05-31 for about $2.5m at an average $77,135, and about 3,588 BTC sold near the end of June 2026 for $216m. Management stated on the Q2 call that it will sell bitcoin whenever it considers doing so advantageous and that investors should expect that on a go-forward basis.

findings.source: Strategy 8-K disclosures reported by CoinDesk 2026-06-01 and subsequently; Q2 2026 earnings call remarks

findings.claim: Funding the full $1,633m annual carry from bitcoin sales at $77,000 consumes 21,208 BTC a year, 2.51% of the stack, taking bitcoin per share from roughly 220,000 sats to 214,485 sats - a 2.51% annual decline, against the +13.3% BTC Yield reported for the first five months of 2026. At bitcoin $45,000 the bleed is 4.3% a year.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.unit: % annual change in bitcoin per share if carry is funded by sales
findings.source: Derived from the Phase 2 carry figure, 845,256 BTC and ~384.2m shares; reported BTC Yield of 13.3% YTD at 2026-05-25 and bitcoin per share of 220,900 sats

findings.claim: Management's headline KPI cannot decline when the strategy fails. BTC Yield was +13.3% year to date at 2026-05-25 with a BTC Gain of 89,378 bitcoin and a BTC $ Gain of $6.8bn, while the bitcoin price fell 12% year to date (from $87,515 at 2025-12-31), leaving bitcoin value per share approximately flat and the shares roughly 65% below their 52-week high. BTC Yield rises whenever stock is issued above 1.0x mNAV regardless of the bitcoin price or the cost of the capital.
findings.label: MANAGEMENT GUIDANCE
findings.source: Strategy company disclosure of BTC Yield, BTC Gain and BTC $ Gain at 2026-05-25; bitcoin price of $87,515 at 2025-12-31 per FY2025 disclosure; 52-week range $81.81-$365.21

findings.claim: Capital raised: $25.3bn in calendar 2025 (largest US equity issuance for a second consecutive year), $11.68bn in the first four months of 2026 (largest US equity issuance of 2026), $8.41bn of ATM proceeds in Q2 2026 and $1.28bn between 1 and 26 July 2026 - followed by a common-ATM pause of roughly ten weeks from mid-June.

findings.claim: The 1 million bitcoin by end-2026 target requires roughly 155,000 more bitcoin, about $12bn at $77,000, in under four months with the common ATM economically shut. It is classified Speculative Demand and carries zero weight in any scenario.

findings.claim: The only clearly value-accretive capital action of 2026 was balance-sheet shrinkage: $1.50bn of 2029 convertible notes repurchased and cancelled for $1.38bn on 2026-05-19, an 8% discount. The software business, worth roughly $1.5bn, could retire a similar amount of 12% preferred and save about $180m a year of carry, and has not been monetised.

findings.source: Strategy press release 2026-05-15 and Q2 2026 10-Q; software valuation is an analyst estimate

findings.claim: Strategy uses no secured borrowing against its bitcoin, which is a genuine credit strength - it cannot be margin-called, and survived a roughly 33% bitcoin drawdown in H1 2026 without a forced sale. It also cannot earn any yield on the asset: bitcoin does not stake, in contrast to the ETH treasury peer BitMine, which funds a dividend from staking yield on more than 4.7m ETH.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.source: Assessment of Strategy's disclosed capital structure (unsecured converts and perpetual preferred only); BitMine staking-funded dividend per treasury-sector reporting, 2026

conclusions: Strategy's committed forward funding is zero: a $42bn ATM authorisation is a permit to offer securities, not a pipeline, while the $1,633m of annual preferred dividends on the other side is contractual and ratcheting.

Common issuance now creates about 2 cents of value per dollar raised after fees at a 1.04x mNAV, down 97% from the 74 cents available at the November 2024 peak, and it turns negative on a 5% share-price fall.

Preferred-funded bitcoin purchases carry an incremental margin of roughly minus 11 percentage points - a ~1% realised asset return against 12% capital. Growth here destroys capital rather than merely diluting returns.

Bitcoin sales to fund dividends are policy, not accident: 32 BTC in May and 3,588 BTC for $216m in June, with management guiding to more. The run-rate bleed is 2.51% of the stack a year, 4.3% at bitcoin $45,000.
The company's headline KPI cannot fall when the strategy fails: BTC Yield was +13.3% year to date while bitcoin value per share was flat and the shares were 65% below their high.

The only value-accretive actions available in 2026 are balance-sheet shrinkage - buying back converts at a discount, and monetising the software business - which is the opposite of the stated strategy.
thesisImpact: Answers Phase 2's question: the $1,633m comes from selling the asset or from issuing more of the instrument that created the obligation. Neither is growth, and both shrink bitcoin per share - the only variable the equity is long. The thesis is now fully specified: MSTR is a levered claim on bitcoin carrying a 2.51% annual fee that rises as bitcoin falls, whose one source of alpha is switched off and cannot restart until the outcome it is meant to cause has already occurred.
